about.body: The Duratorq is a Ford-sourced 2.2-litre four-cylinder diesel engine (Puma family), used in Land Rover applications between 2011 and 2016. It's a chain-driven engine — not a belt — and was fitted across the Defender (late Puma-generation), Discovery Sport, Freelander 2 and Range Rover Evoque. The same engine family was also used in the Ford Transit and Mondeo, though our work here covers Land Rover-badged applications specifically. Across Land Rover, it appears in both TD4 and SD4 variants, with the SD4 carrying a higher power output.

byModel.body: Across the Defender (L663 Puma, 2012–2016), the Duratorq powered the 2.2 TDCi variant during the final years of the classic Defender's production. The Discovery Sport (L550, 2014–2016) used it in TD4 and SD4 form before the Ingenium diesel range replaced it. The Freelander (L359, 2011–2014) carried it as TD4 and SD4 in the final years of Freelander production. The Range Rover Evoque (L538, 2011–2016) also used the Duratorq in TD4 and SD4 variants before the Ingenium engines took over in the L551 generation.

compatibility.body: Because the Duratorq spans four different Land Rover models and multiple generations — some in TD4 form, others in SD4 form — compatibility comes down to confirming your exact model, generation, and drivetrain spec, which we do by registration. A Duratorq from a Defender isn't a drop-in match for a Duratorq from a Range Rover Evoque, even though it's the same base engine family — ancillaries, mounting, and turbo configuration all differ. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm your exact vehicle.
